{{recipesummary|category=Fruit recipes|yield=8 ea. ½-cup servings|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Midwestern cuisine|Midwestern cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Vegetarian cuisine|Vegetarian Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

This is a nice '''applesauce''' to enjoy any time, but especially with [[Cookbook:Latkes|latkes]] during Hanukkah. You don't need to get your blender dirty; you just need a potato masher and a little elbow grease. The use of a sugar substitute makes the applesauce sweeter with less sugar added.

==Ingredients==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (1300 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] / about 8 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) peeled, cored, and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Apple|apples]] 
* ½ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] white [[Cookbook:Sugar|granulated sugar]]
* 6 tablespoons sugar substitute
* Juice from 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] (about 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]])
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|ground cinnamon]] or apple pie spice

==Procedure==
# Put chopped apples in a large [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Stir in water, sugar, sugar substitute, and lemon juice.
# Bring mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boil|boil]], cover, and reduce heat to medium-low.
# Cook until apples are tender (about 10 minutes).
# Use a [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|potato masher]] to break cooked apples up into a nice [[Cookbook:Purée|purée]].
# Stir in ground cinnamon or apple pie spice.
# Serve warm or cold.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Use whatever variety of apples you prefer.
